name: Marine Parade Convenience Store & Beach Shop
Bishop's Bridge Convenience Store & Off Licence
Museum of Norwich at the Bridewell
Smokey Joe's American Bar and Grill
The Maltsters
description: Pub at Ranworth Staithe, steps from the moorings and the boardwalk to the church tower.

name: Reedham Ferry Inn
description: Riverside pub at Reedham with moorings, near the chain ferry and swing bridge.

name: Ranworth Broad Boardwalk
description: 1-mile floating boardwalk through wet woodland to the Broads Wildlife Centre and up St Helen's church tower for the best Broads view. From Ranworth Staithe.

name: How Hill Trails
description: 2½-mile estate & marsh trails past Toad Hole Cottage and the drainage mills. From How Hill moorings on the Ant.

name: Salhouse Broad Woods
description: 2-mile woodland & broad-edge loop — easy and dog-friendly. From Salhouse Broad moorings.

name: Cockshoot Boardwalk & Hide
description: 1½-mile boardwalk to a hide over the conservation broad. From Cockshoot Dyke moorings on the Bure.

name: Coltishall Common Riverside
description: 1½-mile riverside common stroll at the head of navigation — relaxed and good for paddling. Beside the Bure.

name: Thurne Mill & Riverbank
description: 2-mile walk to the white-sailed Thurne Dyke mill and along the riverbank. From Thurne Staithe.

name: Weavers' Way: Stalham to Hickling
description: 6-mile Weavers' Way section from the Stalham (Richardsons) base across the marshes to Hickling — big skies, reedbeds; dogs on leads.

name: Hickling Broad Circular (NWT)
description: 5-mile circular round England's largest broad — marsh harriers, swallowtails, NWT reserve trails. From Hickling Staithe; dogs on leads.

name: Barton Broad, Neatishead & Irstead
description: 5½-mile circular linking Gay's Staithe, Neatishead and thatched Irstead church around Barton Broad.

name: Ludham, How Hill & St Benet's Abbey
description: 6-mile circular from Ludham Bridge taking in How Hill and the ruined St Benet's Abbey — proper big-country marsh walking.

name: Horning to Ranworth (Weavers' Way)
description: 6-mile there-and-back on Weavers' Way from Horning to Ranworth — riverside, woodland and a pub at each end.

name: Reedham to Berney Arms (Wherryman's Way)
description: 7-mile there-and-back on the lonely Wherryman's Way beside the Yare to the remote Berney Arms windmill & pub — vast skies, no roads.

name: Surlingham & Wheatfen (Ted Ellis Reserve)
description: 4½-mile circular through Wheatfen, Ted Ellis's wild fenland reserve, and along the Yare. Dog-friendly.

name: Carlton & Oulton Marshes (SWT)
description: 5-mile circular across Carlton Marshes Suffolk Wildlife Trust reserve from Oulton Broad — grazing marsh, cranes and otters.

name: Whitlingham Country Park Circular
description: 3½-mile family circular round Whitlingham's broads and woods near Norwich — very dog-friendly, café and big meadows.

name: Cantley & Buckenham Marshes (RSPB)
description: 6-mile riverside walk along the Yare past Buckenham & Cantley RSPB marshes — wintering geese and wide grazing levels.

name: Upton Fen & Marshes (NWT)
description: 4-mile circular through Upton Fen's rare wet woodland and dykes from Upton Dyke moorings; dogs on leads near stock.

name: Rockland Broad
description: Renowned coarse-fishing broad off the Yare — pike, bream and roach. Moor at Rockland Staithe and fish the broad or the dyke.

name: Womack Water (Ludham)
description: Quiet dyke off the Thurne with excellent bank fishing from the staithe moorings.

name: Barton Broad
description: The Broads’ second-largest broad — open-water bream and pike. Moor at Gay’s Staithe or Neatishead.

name: Oulton Broad
description: Large broad at Lowestoft with mixed coarse fishing and easy moorings at Nicholas Everitt Park.

name: Salhouse Broad
description: Sheltered broad off the Bure, good for a relaxed afternoon’s float fishing from the moorings.

name: Wroxham Broad
description: The Bure’s biggest broad near Wroxham — open-water bream, roach and pike.

name: Hickling Broad
description: Big shallow broad famed for pike and bream — fish from the staithe. NWT reserve, observe the rules.

name: South Walsham Broad
description: Quiet inner broad off the Bure with sheltered float fishing from the moorings.

name: Surlingham Broad
description: Reed-fringed broad off the Yare near Coldham Hall — classic tench and rudd water.

name: River Bure at Horning
description: Productive river stretch through Horning for roach, bream and big perch from the bank or moored.

name: River Yare at Brundall
description: Deep tidal Yare with bream shoals and the chance of a big pike; fish near the marina moorings.

name: River Waveney at Beccles
description: Slow, wide Waveney through Beccles — roach, bream and chub from the quay moorings.

name: Beccles Lido
description: Family-favourite open-air heated swimming pool right by the Waveney at Beccles — proper safe swimming with a paddling pool and café. Seasonal; check session times. Moor at Beccles.

name: Whitlingham Great Broad
description: Supervised open-water swimming venue near Norwich (Whitlingham Outdoor Education Centre) — sessions must be booked, not free-swim. The only organised open-water swim on the system.

name: Salhouse Broad shallows
description: Shallow, sandy-edged broad sometimes used for paddling and a dip from the moorings — check for blue-green algae warnings and keep well clear of the navigation channel.

name: Rockland Broad (wild dip)
description: A quiet broad off the Yare where confident wild-swimmers occasionally dip away from the channel — cold, weedy and algae-prone, so at your own risk and never near boats.
